title: Rust's Borrow Checker vs Zig's Explicit Allocators
question: Does compile-time lifetime analysis (Rust) or explicit memory allocation without hidden control flow (Zig) offer the better developer model for production systems programming?
points: Rust guarantees memory safety at compile time, eliminating data races and use-after-free without a GC.
Zig avoids macro magic, hidden allocations, and complex borrow checker fighting, offering faster compile times.
Where do you draw the line between developer velocity and formal safety guarantees?

title: Go Goroutines vs Tokio Async Runtimes in Microservices
question: For high-throughput network services, does Go's M:N runtime-managed scheduler beat Rust's explicit zero-cost async/await state machines in real-world maintenance?
points: Go's colored-function-free model makes concurrency accessible and predictable for team velocity.
Tokio in Rust provides zero-allocation futures, strict task cancellation, and avoids GC pause latency.
Which model has your team found more robust under multi-gigabit traffic spikes?

title: SQLite in Production: Has Modern Hardware Made Client-Server DBs Overkill?
question: With modern NVMe drives, WAL mode, and Litestream/LiteFS replication, should SQLite be the default primary database for 90% of web apps instead of PostgreSQL?
points: Zero network latency on queries; no connection pooling overhead or separate database infrastructure.
Single-writer limitation requires careful write transaction design under high concurrent mutations.
At what scale (writes/sec, dataset size) does migrating to Postgres or MySQL become unavoidable?

title: The Modular Monolith vs Microservices in 2026
question: Did the industry over-index on distributed microservices? Are well-bounded modular monoliths superior for engineering velocity and operational sanity?
points: Modular monoliths provide instant in-process refactoring, atomic transactions, and zero RPC network serialization overhead.
Microservices allow independent deployment pipelines and heterogeneous technology stacks for large independent squads.
How does your team enforce strict domain boundaries inside a single codebase?

title: Local Quantized LLMs (Ollama/vLLM) vs Frontier Cloud APIs
question: When building production AI applications, is self-hosting quantized open-weights models (Llama 3, Gemma, Mistral) viable against frontier cloud APIs?
points: Local inference guarantees absolute data privacy, zero API bills, and predictable latency with dedicated VRAM.
Frontier APIs (Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5, GPT-4o) retain a significant reasoning and tool-calling capability gap.
Where is your project's balance between private self-hosted inference and frontier cloud models?

title: Agentic Reasoning Loops vs Deterministic Workflow Engines
question: Should AI agents have autonomous iterative feedback loops (ReAct/Plan-and-Solve), or are strict deterministic state machines with discrete LLM steps more reliable?
points: Autonomous loops adapt dynamically to unexpected edge cases, file revisions, and runtime compilation errors.
Unconstrained loops can enter infinite self-referential rabbit holes and run up unexpected compute costs.
How do you ensure deterministic stopping conditions when orchestrating autonomous agent teams?

title: The Licensing Battle: Permissive (MIT/Apache 2.0) vs Copyleft (GPLv3/AGPL)
question: In the era of cloud providers wrapping open-source tools as managed services, does permissive licensing still protect independent creators?
points: Permissive licenses maximize ecosystem adoption, commercial contributions, and community growth.
Strong copyleft (AGPLv3) forces cloud vendors and derivative creators to contribute source code back to the community.
What license do you choose for your personal and team open-source repositories?
